notes.notes:
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3037660/Robin_Hood_Sherwood_Defenders/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/9074f172663b9489ab8980caf55223efcd7e8379.png[/img][/url]

[b]🏹 The champion of Sherwood's forests returns for another adventure! 🏹[/b]

This time around we're offering [b]an entirely different experience[/b] with our hooded hero. [b]Robin Hood: Sherwood Defenders[/b] is a game inspired by our first title, but the rules change ever so slightly.

💀 As befits evil, [b]the wicked Sheriff of Nottingham never sleeps[/b] and this time he seeks to tighten his grip on the surrounding lands by forcefully securing some of its most precious locations from Robin's most trusted allies. The legendary archer will have none of that! As Sheriff forces march on his friends' homes, [b]Robin takes it upon himself to organize a defensive effort and fend them off for good![/b] 

🏰 In Robin Hood: Sherwood Defenders, you take charge in [b]tower-defense gameplay[/b] – construct [b]walls, gates, and towers[/b] to slow down your foes, [b]production buildings[/b] to sustain more structures and their upgrades with an income of [b]resources[/b], and finally [b]hire soldiers[/b] to have someone at your side when the clash begins. 

🛡️ And you'll need someone at your side indeed! [b]Time is short[/b] and when the [b]enemy wave[/b] comes, there's nothing else for Robin to do but [b]jump right into the thick of it[/b] and give the Sheriff cronies what for himself with his sword and arrows! [b]Score points[/b] for your performance in battle, for which you'll [b]unlock new defenses[/b] in future fights. 

👉 [b]Robin Hood: Sherwood Defenders is not a DLC of Sherwood Builders. It's a standalone game that you can enjoy without having to follow from our previous game's story.[/b]

Stick around with us for announcements about the game's [b]release date[/b]. If you're willing to give it a shot, we'd appreciate you [b]adding the game to your wishlist here on Steam[/b].

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3037660/Robin_Hood_Sherwood_Defenders/

We hope to see you on the battlements!
~ The Robin Hood: Sherwood Builders Team

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/8635830bd6b54e914e55e7d74ea788fdb7094e2e.png[/img]

[h2]The Arena Update![/h2]

[b]A brand new location[/b] is discovered deep within the wilderness surrounding Nottingham. A place of blood sports, where the stakes go really high, whether we're talking coin or lives... [b]Welcome to the Blood Cairn Arena![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/8554f3b345549fe886655772af6d052998d9d658.png[/img]

[h3]Fighting Pit[/h3]
Gamblers travel here from far and wide, fighters of questionable character draw their weapons on its well-trodden ground, spectators cheer loudly, demanding their share of excitement. That's what the Blood Cairn Arena is all about. 
And now Robin can also join the fray in customizeable team fights, during which he either supports his fighters in the melee or from the parapet above, barraging the opponents with arrows and triggering traps.
It's a fight to the death for the ultimate prize!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/c80aa7f54c680b774f6040140deda9d0fa17d1e4.png[/img]

[h3]A Familiar Face[/h3]
But what is the ultimate prize of Blood Cairn? Well, it's not just a high winning bet ever since the arena announced its Grand Tournament. It has drawn a bigger crowd than ever, coming after a phenomenal bounty of gold.
And who does Robin encounter among this crowd? None other than his distant relative, self-proclaimed rival, and master swordsman – [b]Will Scarlet[/b] (Don't call him 'Scarlock'). What kind of predicament is Will going to rope Robin into with this Grand Tournament in full swing?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/33beb78ea43ec727c84b45ba361ee2de10dd0f94.png[/img]

[b]Visit the Blood Cairn Arena for the fight of your life today! Check Robin's house in the Village for hints on where to find it.[/b]

[list]

- Betting feature in the arena as a source of coin income

notes.title: Manufacture Update – Now available!
notes.notes:
🏹[b]Greetings, Sherwood Builders![/b]⛺

The "Manufacture Update", our second content addition to the game is now available!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/7a482402cb5e8cd8d3d432ab8c1853df920c3690.png[/img]

[h3]Remember – the update allows you to continue your game with your previous saves![/h3]

With the Manufacture Update, we're expanding our building selection for Robin's Village. From now on, there are several new buildings belonging to the decorative and production categories. Now you can do even more to spruce up your hideout! One of these – not entirely a building per se – even comes with a little sweet surprise. 🍎 As for the two new production buildings, they are intended to make your efforts in obtaining certain resources a little easier if you're willing to invest a bit in their construction.

But apart from the above, we're introducing further fixes and adjustments to make your experience with the game more enjoyable – improved lighting and lip-sync animations for characters to make the game's world even more lifelike as well as further changes to combat for better play with, for example, fights that involve blocking and multiple participants.

Here's a comprehensive list of changes in the Manufacture Update, bringing the game to version 4.04.24.01:
[list]
[*] Added new Decorative category buildings to the Village Builder (with one rather helpful tree among them),
[*] Added new Production category buildings: the Butcher and the Garden for more convenient generation of certain resources and usable items,
[*] Added lip-sync animation to make the game's characters more lifelike,
[*] Improved icons for buildings in the Village Builder,
[*] Added toggle for point light shadows in graphics settings,
[*] Global adjustments to lighting in the overland and various locations,
[*] Added visual effect that indicates when Robin is hidden in tall grass,
[*] Rebalanced Robin's attacks and enemy abilities, as well as adjusted the mechanics of enemy shields for a better combat experience,
[*] Expanded system of enemy aggro to better work with group fights,
[*] Various AI adjustments and optimizations.
[*] Various enhancements to the game's sound effects, improving the overall audio experience,
[*] Fixed bug related to errors caused by weapon swapping,
[*] Various localization fixes.
[/list]

Let us know in the comments what you think about our changes. Stick with Robin's Merry Men to see what's to come!

Stay vigilant,
MeanAstronauts Team

notes.title: Core Update – Now available!
notes.notes:
🏹[b]Good day to you, Sherwood Builders![/b]⛺

Our first major update, which we've dubbed the "Core Update", is now available! We've been carefully reading your reviews and listening to your feedback and, ever since the game's release, working hard to further improve your experience with it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/c3e6430d1fd1ef5c2102255bc913ab20465aa988.png[/img]

[h3]Remember – the update allows you to continue your game with your previous saves![/h3]

With the Core Update, we primarily aim to provide Robin with more attacks from the start of the game, so that [b]its combat immediately becomes more dynamic[/b], rather than requiring, for example, progression in the Village Builder before the attack skills contributing to dynamic combat are unlocked. Incidentally, this required rebalancing for the skill upgrades.

Changes like these belong to several of the update's adjustments that intend to improve the overall quality of life and balancing of the game, [b]but that's not all. The Core Update also includes some new features[/b]: a special strong attack for Robin to overwhelm his foes, a friendly NPC to spar with, a new voice for Friar Tuck, and many more!

With this update, the game also becomes available with [b]Brazilian Portuguese localization[/b]!

Here's a comprehensive list of changes in the Core Update, bringing the game to version 4.03.26.01:
[list]
[*] Increased Robin's combat responsiveness by unlocking more active attack skills from the start of the game, adjusting their progression, and by enabling regular attacks in situations when no special attack is yet unlocked,
[*] Added a new strong attack for Robin that you can perform by holding down the normal attack input, which gives you an option from the start of the game to deliver a lot of damage at once, break the enemy's block, and potentially stun them. It is, however, slower and costs some extra Energy,
[*] Added new friendly NPC to Robin's Village, with whom you can practice combat,
[*] Added the item sort feature to containers,
[*] Added Brazilian Portuguese localization,
[*] Added the Sprint Mode setting to the start of the game, where you can choose to either toggle Robin's sprint or keep it active as long as the relevant input is pressed down. The Sprint Mode setting is still available in the Settings menu as previously.
[*] Added gamma setting to the game's graphics settings,
[*] Added the possibility to move the camera while placing buildings in the Village Builder,
[*] Added extra instructions related to combat in Robin's house,
[*] Added various adjustments for general audio improvement,
[*] Added indicators to compass markers that inform you whether a given object or character is above or below Robin,
[*] Added NPCs to Village buildings to liven the place up a little,
[*] Friar Tuck has a brand new voice!
[*] Rebalancing related to Repair Kit costs, attack skills, and some trader inventories (Wire has been added to hunter-type traders and Gypsum can now be bought from general-type traders and in Robin's Village),
[*] Rebalancing related to maximum item durability, where all items' max durability has been greatly increased (current durability of already created items will be retained, so they will have to be repaired if needed),
[*] Fixed bug related to the "Conquer Conisbrough Castle" quest, where it wouldn't be possible to progress the quest after leaving the convoy area. The convoy will now be available again when you return and you'll be able to finish the quest.
[*] Fixed bug related to the experience progression bar in Robin's character screen not being displayed,
[*] Fixed bug related to fog persisting after leaving the Nottingham area,
[*] Fixed bug related to custom map marker disappearing when zooming map,
[*] Various localization fixes,
[*] Various small bugfixes related to glitches in locations and quest progression.
[/list]

Let us know in the comments what you think about our changes. Anything else you'd really like to see in Sherwood Builders? We continue working on the game to further improve it, with big plans of new features, so do be here with us in the Outlaws' Village to see what's to come!

Good hunting,

[h3]📣 Greetings, Sherwood Builders! 🏹[/h3]

[b]To celebrate the release of Robin Hood - Sherwood Builders this Thursday on February 29th, you are invited to join us for our second live broadcast on launch day at 8:55 AM EST / 1:55 PM UTC![/b] We'll be playing Sherwood Builders right where the prologue leaves off. The broadcast will appear on the game's Steam page.

Just as we wrote about the ruthless bandits belonging to the Sons of Adam faction in our last devlog, today we present a group with its own brand of ruthlessness – the Forest Spirits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/0e3e7ca06cf0d247b22bc9fc14b43192bf9c254b.png[/img]

The Forest Spirits are a numerous group of bandits with unmistakeable characteristics. They're wild men, in many senses of the word. [b]They don animal pelts, wield axes, and have howls for battle cries.[/b] This behavior is easily explained by how deeply they draw from their norse berserker heritage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/1184e948636682a03343ee5123f1046e15df9158.png[/img]

This faction's members are rarely ever just a nuisance but rather always a notably serious threat. The lawlesness of the land's rulers has been conducive to their own barbaric regression, and so [b]Forest Spirits can be encountered in various Regions, raiding, reaving, and pillaging, much like their Viking ancestors did.[/b] Strength and ruthlesness in combat is what determines one's value in their society, so don't ever presume that diplomacy is an option when you run into them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/e34a5b3e3eed437583843d9657afe11d1354c7a3.png[/img]

[b]But absolutely do not ever mistake their primitivism for stupidity.[/b] Forest Spirits are close to nature, they have their means and traditions of survival, outside of brutality and taking what they need by force, of course. This often translates to knowing which berries are safe to eat as much as which plants you can stuff in a cauldron to brew what are essentially alchemical grenades. If Robin is ever struck by such concoctions, he not only has to deal with poison damage over time, but also some surprising side effects. Be on your guard.

[b]We hope to see you take on the bandits on February 29th when the full version of Robin Hood - Sherwood Builders is released![/b]

This is not only because of the royal soldiers, still fully loyal to the despot, but because of the questionable allies he made while establishing himself as the land's ruler. Bandits, renegades, outcasts, and all manner of unsavory characters form different enemy factions in Sherwood Builders, all too ready to do the Sheriff's bidding for their own benefit and stand in Robin's way. Today, let's talk about...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/a34f45b80fbd6f3016ee958fbfb3f0679423a7fd.png[/img]

To describe the Sons of Adam in one word, they are bandits. As bandit as anyone can get, but with a particularly unpleasant twist. Led by one Adam Coterel, with his two brothers serving as the group's lieutenants, they take to theft, robbery, and all other manner of criminal activity, very often in service to  their associates, to further their personal interests through destruction and intimidation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/48aa229116bfaccb0cf2be6e5d0acf9f026d3b8c.png[/img]

This particular faction doesn't enjoy an exceptional degree of organization, which makes the task of taking it on possible, but also brings with it tragic consequences to the people of Nottingham – The Sons of Adam are brutal, savage, and resort to exceptionally cruel methods of running their criminal operations. They tend to commit truly evil atrocities, giving Robin even more motivation to oppose them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/19fb7a1815a9031629ffc161256a3661b455cfb6.jpg[/img]

The Sons of Adam appear ragged, with bones, scraps, and their iconic heraldry adorning their outfits and camps. They are quite ubiquitous as far as their presence around the Regions goes. You can encounter them just about anywhere, ready to opportunistically prey on the defenseless. With the Sons of Adam furthering their cause through utter cruelty, it's up to Robin to put a stop to their vicious ways.

To maintain variety in the game's world, we've introduced all sorts of natural settings into it, including:
[list]
[*] Verdant forests, dense with all manner of foliage
[*] Rolling hills and fields stretching as far as the eye can see 
[*] English moors in full bloom
[*] Treacherous swamps for the most daring adventurer
[*] Well-travelled rocky tracts filled with opportunity for the industrious outlaw

Different environments are not only pleasing to the eye, but also significant to the gameplay. [b]Depending on where you travel, you can find different resources to harvest.[/b] Make sure to explore and discover more information about them through in-game readables!

[*] Peak District
[*] Sherwood Forest
[*] Midlands
[/list]

Though he has his Merry Men at his side, he'll still need help from the rightful rulers of the Regions, similarly threatened by the Crown's cruelty. Robin gains [b]Reputation[/b], specific to each of these Regions, by completing quests and helping the people. notes.title: Devlog #8 - Passive Skill Tree
notes.notes:
[h3]📣 Hello, Sherwood Builders! 🏹[/h3]

If you've been following our game for some time now, it's become more than obvious that during his quest to liberate Nottingham and its surrounding lands, Robin Hood is going to face a vast number of threats. These threats will grow in severity the closer Robin draws to deposing the Sheriff. How not to get overwhelmed by your foes? One thing you have to take advantage of is the... 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/2316433dca626cfecd0cc20bf4483156ee702578.png[/img]

As Robin gains experience points in the game through various means, such as vanquishing his enemies in combat, he eventually gains levels, and with levels come skill points. These can be spent in a special window of the game's menu called the Passive Skills. It's a branching grid that provides an overview of Robin's general abilities and characteristics. Spending skill points here allows you to decide how these advantages are going to be developed. 

In order to better navigate the available options for character improvements, the tree is separated into several sections, called paths:

[list][*][b]Path of the Blade[/b] – This section mainly includes passive skills that simply increase Robin's raw damage output, whether through the enhancement of regular and special attacks or overcoming your enemies' defences. It also offers some good investments if you're interested in keeping Robin capable of swinging his weapon for longer before he gets winded.
[*][b]Path of Craftsmanship[/b] – Multiple passive skills that specialize in improving resource extraction from the various nodes of Sherwood Builders' world. Also a good area if you'd like to conserve your tools more effectively and increase your carry weight capacity.
[*][b]Path of the Arrow[/b] – A ranged equivalent of the Path of the Blade, albeit with a few additional intricacies. The price of being able to attack your opponents from a distance is the necessity to have better control over the various conditions for using a bow. With a little extra time put into consideration, these passives should help tailor your archery to your needs.
[*][b]Path of Endurance[/b] – Survival is the name of the game and the base health and damage resistance boosts from this part of the tree should help with it indeed, especially on higher difficulties. Seeing as some enemies in Sherwood Builders resort to special damage type attacks, certain passives here may eventually prove to be a necessity.
[*][b]Path of Shadows[/b] – The branch of stealth. These passive skills help you stay hidden more effectively when sneaking, but also make you a more effective assassin with improved execution damage and enemy level threshold for an assassination attempt. Some of these even provide utility by enhancing Robin's Hunter Vision ability.
[*][b]Path of Dexterity[/b] – Passive skills which improve Robin's movement. Speed, whether simply travelling or already in combat, but, what may be even more interesting, provide enhancements to critical strikes and penetrating enemy armor. What's not to love?[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/f266493f5a9ab1c2621eabacc69d39a2a53b7f26.jpg[/img]

You'll notice that many of the passive skills in the tree offer miscellaneous utility along the way, regardless of the path in which they're placed. These are sure to prove worthy of your attention as well! 

We can't wait to see what clever builds for Robin you will all come up with as the game launches, but whatever your choices, we hope you'll enjoy your adventure!

notes.title: Devlog #7 - Village Builder
notes.notes:
[h3]📣 Hello, Sherwood Builders! 🏹[/h3]

Starting from scratch is often a difficult predicament, one that Robin Hood and the Merry Men face in Sherwood Builders as they're doomed to a life on the run from the Sheriff. But that doesn't discourage them. The brave outlaws found a hideout concealed deep in the woods of Barnsdale and it's up to Robin to help make it grow and bring aid to the oppressed people of Nottingham's surrounding lands, and to do that, he needs to become a...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/a435d1341fab43c8434a8afa26b891a02b7f9e1c.png[/img]

The game's [b]Builder Mode[/b] allows you to construct your own hideout village, complete with various structures that fulfil a range of functions. Expanding this base provides many [b]benefits[/b]:

[list]
[*][b]Resource production[/b] – A lot of raw materials found in the game's world can also be produced right in Robin's village for easy collection from its Storage after a certain amount of time. Invest right and you might not have to forage as much.
[*][b]Crafting[/b] – Not all item production can be done by hand. If Robin's to upgrade his gear, he'll need the right workshop.
[*][b]Training[/b] – Another category of buildings will allow Robin to improve his various skills, both those related to combat and not.
[*][b]Decorating[/b] – Surely, many don't want their creation to be bland and strictly just functional. The denizens of Robin's hideout will feel much better if you add a touch of aesthetics to the community with some decorative elements.
[/list]
All the advantages don't come with no effort and if you wish to reap the benefits of the [b]Builder Mode[/b], you'll need to face several [b]challenges[/b] as well:
[list]
[*][b]Caring for the people[/b] – All the fruits of your village's labour won't come from thin air. You need people loyal to your cause to put their backs into it. Recruit new villagers from the surrounding lands through various events, house them, feed them, and give them jobs if you want your hideout running the way you picture it.
[*][b]Securing the materials[/b] – Buildings are not only constructed, but also upgraded. The more advanced your structures the better the advantages you can gain from them. But progress 'will' require increasingly more sophisticated resources. Secure them first while campaigning through the Regions and maybe you'll afford yourself the opportunity to generate them yourself later.
[*][b]Space management[/b] – It may seem like you have the whole forest to yourself, but a hideout won't be quite that hidden if it just sprawls endlessly. There's technically enough room to secure all the Merry Men's needs and also get creative, but first you'll need to wrest it from the thick forest by cutting down its trees.
[/list][previewyoutube=OavagAjRCwc;full][/previewyoutube]
Robin's village is essential to progressing through the game, but we've made sure all the rules of this gameplay aspect are transparent and the interface for managing everything for it is easy to follow with the right stats and indicators. We can't wait to see your versions of the hideout!

notes.title: Devlog #6 - Stealth
notes.notes:
[h3]📣 Hello, Sherwood Builders! 🏹[/h3]

Yuletide is just around the corner. Countless merrymakers around the world get into the spirit of gift-giving, so do we bring you fresh development news about Sherwood Builders all the while wishing you all the best for the upcoming Holidays! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/3dc6392fcfa5393aeae52fa1c59d7f01627895b0.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/5df6477d4b6496e856da9a17c9513a7e3091bbef.png[/img]

[b][h3]Stealth[/h3][/b]

Stealth builds, sneaking mechanics, critical surprise attacks. We've all seen the many different ways in which stealth mechanics are employed in games, so it stands to reason that Sherwood Builders, a game about outlaws in hiding, just wouldn't do without them.

Invest your skill points, gained by levelling up, in various portions of Robin's skill tree that will enhance his stealth-related abilities and offer you unique challenges, which will be well rewarded if you do everything right. Mind the amount of noise you're making with your movement speed or veil yourself in night's darkness to further improve your chances.

[b]Stealth benefits:[/b]
[list][*][b]Go unnoticed:[/b] Not every direct confrontation can be won, not every odds will be in Robin's favor. Sometimes the best course of action for accomplishing your objective is to avoid the fight altogether and well-developed stealth abilities will enable you just that.
[*][b]Eliminate enemies:[/b] Few things are as satisfying as thrusting defeat on your foes before they even realize they're in a fight. Sneaking in Sherwood Builders enables you to instantly kill enemies in melee assassination or dropping down on hostile characters from above. It can also significantly increase damage with arrows when they're fired at unaware opponents. Beware, however! If your target's level greatly outweighs Robin's, the assassination will fail, with damage dealt as your only benefit of the attempt.
[*][b]Seize treasures:[/b] Not all valuables lie out in the open. Sneaking around, breaking locks, and taking down security mechanisms will be the only way of getting your hands on them. A stealthy burglar will witness many rewards as they complete the many, many Sherwood Builders quests.[/list]
[b]Stealth challenges:[/b]
[list][*][b]Risk of discovery:[/b] The closer you are to enemies, the higher the risk of being noticed. Sneaking requires caution and patience, as carelessness may end unpleasantly for you. Do this correctly and make sure you upgrade your skills well or you may find yourself suddenly surrounded by enemies eager to fight you and well aware of your presence. Keep a 'plan B' on hand.
[*][b]Using the environment:[/b] Stealth means a demand for perfect awareness of your surroundings. You have to use your surroundings to your advantage by hiding in dense foliage and behind objects to remain unseen and staying still if you're making too much noise. Your Hunter Vision ability will prove useful to find out which way your enemies are looking and whether they can hear you. Study their patrol routes carefully if you want to pull it off.
[*][b]Skill investment:[/b] How well you sneak about is not a finite deal, not by a long shot. The 'Path of Shadows' part of Robin's skill tree features many upgrades to how you can take advantage of the game's stealth features. If you want to reap the benefits, the challenge lies in choosing the right options between levelling up stealth skills and Robin's other abilities, such as those related to combat and crafting. [/list]

We hope that the sneaking mechanics in Robin Hood - Sherwood Builders will provide you with even greater excitement and challenges. We encourage you to share your impressions and suggestions on our community forum. Thank you for your support, and we're already working on further enhancements!

And keep following us for a more precise date in a news post to come!

[h3]Gameplay Difficulty in Sherwood Builders[/h3]

Many games don't manage their difficulty design in a fair way, especially when it comes to combat. This is mostly done by having the difficulty setting modify the stats of characters and creating so-called damage sponges – enemies who force you into a slog of being battered for a long period of time until they're finally defeated. While at it, the fight doesn't offer much in the way of new combat gameplay and only either shorterns or lengthens the loop that's already in place.

We wanted a different approach, one that would address gameplay challenge through combat and, consequently, actually mean something to the player. And so, the three different difficulty levels of Sherwood Builders: Rogue, Outlaw, and Legend affect the way enemies behave alongside several other combat-related conditions:
[list]
[*] Damage caused by enemies
[*] Frequency of enemy attacks
[*] Number of enemies willing to attack at the same time
[*] Chances of various enemy responses, such as blocking and dodging
[*] The rate at which Robin gets fatigued by fighting
[*] The timing window for the player to parry attacks
[*] Item drop chances
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39647153/139a99cbb1a3af8e1699d1e0dd6c46c68b602051.gif[/img]

notes.title: Robin Hood: Sherwood Builders puts city-building in a survival RPG, and the demo's a hit
notes.notes:
We're reaching the end of Steam Next Fest, which means your fellow PC gamers have had the chance to see what's good - and judging by what's been topping the charts, it looks like Robin Hood: Sherwood Builders is the surprise hit of the event. It's proven to be a winning combination of RPG games, survival games, and city-building games.

The early bits of the demo play out pretty much like any modern survival adventure - gather some food and resources, and craft your way to new tools. But pretty soon, you'll be putting those resources into a central coffer for your village, then asking your villagers to put together new buildings to expand the settlement.

Eventually, you'll start recruiting new residents, and you can streamline your way past the traditional survival mechanics by robbing convoys for resources. All along the way, you're guided by a dialogue-heavy series of quests featuring characters from the Robin Hood mythos.
